question: Whether the change from 52,466 game production/distribution workers in 2012 to 40,541 in 2013 has a documented KOCCA/MCST methodological cause, and whether 2010-2014 is a proven continuous frame.
answer: No decisive original-method evidence was recovered that attributes the 2012-2013 change to a classification, sampling-frame, collection, contractor-treatment, or revision change. The recovered sources establish consistent source labels and a source-native overlapping historical comparison, but do not prove unchanged survey construction. Do not assert that the 22.7% fall is real employment change or a known methodological break.

source_native_evidence.locator: 2013 White Paper on Korean Games / 2013 Content Industry Statistics extract, PDF p. 9, printed p. 25, Table 4 'Number of game-industry employees (2010-2012)', row 'game production and distribution'.
source_native_evidence.what_it_proves: The 2010-2012 output is a people headcount that separates game production/distribution from PC cafes, arcade-game rooms and video-game venues.

source_native_evidence.locator: 2016 Copyright Protection Annual Report, PDF p. 133 / printed p. 105, Table II-8 'Domestic game-industry worker count (2012-2014)', row 'game production and distribution'; source note credits KOCCA, 2015 White Paper on Korean Games, October 2015.
source_native_evidence.what_it_proves: A government-hosted reproduction presents 2012 52,466, 2013 40,541 and 2014 39,221 in one KOCCA-attributed table, using the same core row and separately showing game circulation/consumption venues. It supports the source-native existence of the reported step between 2012 and 2013.

source_native_evidence.locator: 2017 White Paper on Korean Games, PDF/printed p. 12, Table 5 'Number of game industry employees (2014-2016)', 'Game development/distribution firms - Sub Total'.
source_native_evidence.what_it_proves: Direct KOCCA/MCST publication independently confirms 2014 39,221 and maintains the production/distribution versus circulation/consumption (PC Bang and arcade room) split.

consistent_observed_elements: Core production/development-distribution row is tabulated separately from PC cafes and arcade-game rooms/venues.
2012 overlap is exactly 52,466 in the 2013 KOCCA table and the 2015-White-Paper reproduction; 2014 overlap is 39,221 in the reproduction and direct 2017 KOCCA/MCST White Paper.
not_recovered: The original KOCCA 2015 White Paper methodology appendix or questionnaire/frame documentation.
A KOCCA/MCST statement that 2013's 40,541 is caused by a change in classification, survey universe, response model, or worker-status definition.
A statement that the 2010-2014 survey frames, contractor treatment and exclusion rules were unchanged.
methodological_finding.interpretation: The numerical overlaps make the five values a coherent source-native historical comparison, but not a proven longitudinal frame. The falls can be shown as values reported by the source; causality and comparability remain unproved.

plot_decision.allowed: Five individual 2010-2014 source-native markers, or a deliberately labelled dashed historical comparison segment reading 'KOCCA reported game production/distribution workers; survey-frame continuity not independently established'. Keep production/distribution separate from venue-inclusive totals.
not_allowed: A normal solid trend line whose implied continuity treats the 2012-2013 difference as real workforce contraction.
A causal annotation saying the drop was caused by a documented methodological change or by actual job losses.
Joining the 2010-2014 historical values to the later KR_core line as one unqualified series.
Combining the core row with PC cafes or arcade-game-room workers.
plot_decision.recommended_caption: KOCCA-reported game production/distribution workers. 2010-2014 source-native historical comparison; collection-frame continuity and worker-status treatment not recovered.

main_decision: Retain marker-only presentation. Matching reported values across overlapping source tables are verified, but do not promote optional dashed comparison to a trend. Main rechecked local source extracts.

subsequent_evidence.summary: KOCCA-issued press release directly confirms 2013 value and publication sample of 226 production/distribution firms. Does not resolve cause or survey-frame continuity. Earlier 2009 marker separately proposed.
